sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Best guide and build for Zhezhi from WW (Wuthering Waves). Zhezhi is a 5 ★ rarity character from the Glacio element who uses the Rectifier type weapon.
 Zhezhi is a commissioned painter, quiet and shy with a dedication to her craft. She's not very eloquent, but her persistence and love for painting speak volumes.

 To learn more about Zhezhi check the sections below. Use the tabs to quickly switch to the kind of information you're looking for.

sections.heading: Pros
sections.text:
Has one of the strongest off-field damage outputs in the game (barring full-fledged off-field Main DPS characters like Phrolova).

 Very quick rotation that can be easily improved via Jump Cancels for solid damage and good buffs.

 Very accessible weapon options, not Signature reliant at all.

 Super consistent - attacks from a very far range and teleports around, almost never gets hit by enemies after her Basic chain and first Skill/Heavy Attack cast.

 Provides extra Energy to the incoming character via her Inherent Skill on Outro, making Energy requirements easier to meet.

sections.heading: Cons
sections.text:
Lower damage ceiling overall compared to modern Hybrid characters, and generally lower, more niche buffing profile - easily replaced and outclassed in all teams barring Jinhsi, who is long since powercrept (in a very direct manner too by Luuk Herssen who Zhezhi does not work with).

 Low headroom for quickswap; her only quickswap window is during her Basic 3.

 Like most version 1 characters, has terrible sequence scaling, meaning they really aren’t worthwhile pickups.

 Moonlit Clouds can be awkward to use by nature of Impermanence Heron being a Transform Echo, making her default to Empyrean Anthem for comfort where high stats are a necessity for the set to be worth it.

sections.heading: Review
sections.text: Zhezhi is a 5-star Glacio Rectifier Hybrid who focuses on buffing Glacio and Resonance Skill damage while having the aptitude to do off-field damage. Specializing in relatively quick on-field combos followed by off-field Coordinated Attacks, she will provide constant damage support both when she’s on and when she’s off the field, able to not only buff your characters but also provide a decent source of on and off-field single-target damage. This defines her core use cases and playstyle.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics
sections.text:
All of Zhezhi’s gameplay revolves around her Forte gauge, which allows her to accumulate up to 3 stacks called Afflatus. Generated through her Intro Skill and Basic Attacks, her Forte gauge has 3 segments for a total of 90 Afflatus points, 30 points per stack.
 Once a segment is full, Zhezhi can convert it into a Phantasmic Imprint using specific abilities. These Phantasmic Imprints are teleport points visible on the field that Zhezhi will teleport to and deal damage with, while generating a lot of Concerto Energy when she uses her Resonance Skill with Phantasmic Imprints placed and ready to activate on the field.
 She can convert the segments in two ways: using her base Resonance Skill, which can convert up to 2 segments, and her Forte Heavy Attack (which can be triggered immediately by performing a Basic Attack after her Resonance Skill), which can convert the last segment when her Forte gauge is full. In case she gets interrupted on that attack however, she may cast it via a Heavy following a teleport Skill as well, provided she has enough Forte to consume.
 With all of the above information, Zhezhi’s rotation becomes clear: She may rotate by activating her Intro skill, filling 1.5 segments of her Forte gauge, then completing a full Basic Attack sequence, filling out the remaining 1.5 segments, using her Resonance Skill and Forte Heavy Attack to convert them all into Imprints, which she will teleport to in quick succession, finishing with her Echo before finally being able to give her 20% Glacio, 25% Skill DMG Amplify Outro to the Main DPS to boost their damage. Her Outro skill has the additional effect of restoring Resonance Energy to the character you switch into - something that is very desired on both DPS characters she typically supports, Carlotta and Jinhsi.
 The gameplay she sports looks fundamentally extremely simplistic - and that statement describes how Zhezhi plays out very accurately. Her ease of use is one of her big selling points, and the above sequence of actions is easy to remember and execute while being quite fast and close to optimal (though it can be optimized via Jump Cancels).
 From a meta standpoint, Zhezhi is nowadays powercrept because she supports powercrept damage dealers. Resonance Skill amplifiers are scarce and the alternatives are bottom tiers in the form of Lumi and Taoqi, but general buffers like Lynae overtake Zhezhi’s spot on most teams outside of her unique use case with Jinhsi since she necessitates Coordinated Attacks. Her ease of use and rare Resonance Skill damage buffing ability make her a strong contender for Jinhsi and Carlotta, but those DPS characters have long since been overshadowed by more recent ones, like Luuk and Hiyuki in the same elements for example.
 In conclusion, even though Zhezhi is one of the very rare choices for Glacio & Skill damage dealers, a lack of something that makes her stand out like strong personal damage, a lightning fast rotation time or high buffing potential make her an overshadowed buffer for DPS characters who are long since

 93.80%

 Yinlin's Signature Rectifier is easily one of the best generalist options in the game, giving Zhezhi a nice but short-lived ATK% buff that can apply to some Coordinated Attacks and the most damaging part of her on-field rotation. However, buffs run out quickly which make it not as ideal as her Signature while still being a completely excellent replacement.
 87.60%

 Calculation also applicable to Luminous Hymn. Simple ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Zhezhi, who does not benefit from this weapon's Fusion Burst and Tune Strain-oriented effects.
 84.60%

 Cosmic Ripples (R 5 )

 Best permanently available option for all Rectifier damage dealers, granting a scaling Basic DMG Bonus buff, some Energy Regen and a massive amount of ATK. Not as ideal as above options due to the absence of CRIT in the stats this weapon grants, but still a capable alternative.
 81.10%

 Augment (R 5 )

 Best 4-star weapon option, this Battle Pass Exclusive gets an easy-to-activate ATK buff when casting Ultimate and also gives a nice CRIT secondary stat but has lower Base ATK as a 4-star making it worse than any 5-star option.
 78.10%

 Radiant Dawn (R 5 )

 Another good Battle Pass Exclusive that grants ATK and Basic DMG when casting Skill, not as ideal as any 5-star due to low Base ATK but also gives CRIT DMG on its secondary stat, making it a decent choice overall albeit easily replaced.
 73.80%

 Fusion Accretion (R 5 )

 Grants some flat Energy when casting Skill and otherwise only gives some decent ATK increases. Replace this weapon when possible, but decent placeholder until 5-star options are acquired.
 69.20%

 Jinzhou Keeper (R 5 )

 Similarly to Fusion Accretion, best no-gacha option accessible at the start of the game but gives nothing except ATK and should be replaced as soon as possible.

sections.heading: Best Echo Sets
sections.text:
1

Empyrean Anthem

 Offers an unconditional 10% Energy Regen% and 80% Coordinated DMG boost. Also grants a passive supportive effect which triggers when the wearer of this set critically strikes with a Coordinated attack - this effect grants the on field Resonator an ATK% boost regardless if they're the wearer of the set or not. The set is better than Moonlit Clouds if and only if the equipped character's Echoes have endgame investment (with 9 or 10 CRIT substats total) and the character has a 5-star weapon equipped. If both conditions aren't met, Moonlit Clouds is a better choice.
 Below you can find Main Echo options:

 Nightmare: Lampylumen Myriad

 - The best Echo for Zhezhi when running the Empyrean Anthem set as it grants her an extra Glacio and Coordinated Attack DMG boost when equipped in the main slot, without taking up rotation time as it is a simple Summon Echo.

 2

Moonlit Clouds

 Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.
 Below you can find Main Echo options:

 Impermanence Heron

 - Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

sections.heading: Rotation
sections.text: Zhezhi’s primary rotation goal is to fill her Forte gauge to then cast her Skill, Heavy Attack, finally teleport with her Skill 3 times, and Outro. She is free to cast her Ultimate at any point in this rotation.

sections.heading: Echo timing
sections.text: Right before Outro (for Moonlit + Impermanence Heron, may require a Dash Cancel on the last Creation’s Zenith Skill), or at any point in the rotation (for Empyrean Anthem + Nightmare: Lampylumen Myriad).

sections.heading: Standard Rotation
sections.text:
Intro

 Basic 1

 Basic 2

 Basic 3

 Skill

 Heavy: Conjuration

 Skill: Stroke of Genius (Jump Cancel)

 Skill: Stroke of Genius (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

 Ultimate

 Skill: Creation’s Zenith (Dash cancel into Echo, Swap, Outro on Moonlit Clouds OR Swap and Outro on Empyrean Anthem)

 Outro

sections.heading: Possible Optimizations & No Ultimate Rotation
sections.text:
Without Ultimate available, an extra Basic 123 into Skill (Swap) before Outro may be necessary in order to get Zhezhi’s Outro properly. This is necessary in later rotations of Jinhsi + Zhezhi teams, but will not see use in Carlotta teams.
 Finally, Zhezhi’s only further optimizations than what we listed above, can be to use her Ultimate as early as possible in Jinhsi teams (this means another Jump Cancel will need to be timed properly on the second Skill cast otherwise Zhezhi will be sent flying up into the air and lose time which makes it riskier), and her Basic 123 chain can be cast before Intro and Basic 3 can be Swap Cancelled to save more time as well (this allows Zhezhi to Intro and cast her Skill immediately afterwards, making the rotation more consistent and saving time overall).
 Lastly, on Moonlit Clouds, her Echo may be cast before her rotation starts if you have that much headroom for Swap Cancels available (generally not realistic in Carlotta and Jinhsi team rotations beyond the Opener rotation however).

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Carlotta Jinhsi Lingyang - These are the DPS choices where Zhezhi is most valuable. While she can function as a Hybrid for teams like Hiyuki+Chisa to buff Hiyuki's Glacio DMG for example, Zhezhi shines at her best in teams that can fully utilize her Outro skill or benefit from her Coordinated Attacks. Her DPS of choice to pair with since version 2.0 has been Carlotta, who utilizes her entire array of buffs to the fullest; but since her release, she's also been Jinhsi's best partner by virtue of being the only Coordinated Attacker who rotates fast without the need for her Ultimate to complete a rotation, while amplifying Skill DMG. Lingyang is also acceptable as a fallback option if the team is built well and Lingyang's optimal playstyle is mastered - in those situations, it may suffice to clear endgame content.
 The Shorekeeper Verina - Since Zhezhi is a generalist Glacio/Skill Amplifier and Coordinated Attack secondary damage dealer, she works best with Supports that increase damage generally, Shorekeeper and Verina being the two best generalists in the game to date as later Support releases got more and more specialized.

sections.heading: Example Teams
sections.text:
Best Team

 Verina can be equal to Shorekeeper in Jinhsi teams with enough crit-fishing (particularly with S2 Verina). Other options under specific circumstances may include Hiyuki+Chisa, or Mornye as a general Support at S1 and above (or R4 Discord and above as a Verina alternative).

 Pros & Cons
 Pros
 Has one of the strongest off-field damage outputs in the game (barring full-fledged off-field Main DPS characters like Phrolova).

 Very quick rotation that can be easily improved via Jump Cancels for solid damage and good buffs.

 Very accessible weapon options, not Signature reliant at all.

 Cons
 Lower damage ceiling overall compared to modern Hybrid characters, and generally lower, more niche buffing profile - easily replaced and outclassed in all teams barring Jinhsi, who is long since powercrept (in a very direct manner too by Luuk Herssen who Zhezhi does not work with).

 Low headroom for quickswap; her only quickswap window is during her Basic 3.

 Review
 Zhezhi is a 5-star Glacio Rectifier Hybrid who focuses on buffing Glacio and Resonance Skill damage while having the aptitude to do off-field damage. Specializing in relatively quick on-field combos followed by off-field Coordinated Attacks, she will provide constant damage support both when she’s on and when she’s off the field, able to not only buff your characters but also provide a decent source of on and off-field single-target damage. This defines her core use cases and playstyle.
 Key Mechanics
 All of Zhezhi’s gameplay revolves around her Forte gauge, which allows her to accumulate up to 3 stacks called Afflatus. Generated through her Intro Skill and Basic Attacks, her Forte gauge has 3 segments for a total of 90 Afflatus points, 30 points per stack.
 Once a segment is full, Zhezhi can convert it into a Phantasmic Imprint using specific abilities. These Phantasmic Imprints are teleport points visible on the field that Zhezhi will teleport to and deal damage with, while generating a lot of Concerto Energy when she uses her Resonance Skill with Phantasmic Imprints placed and ready to activate on the field.
 She can convert the segments in two ways: using her base Resonance Skill, which can convert up to 2 segments, and her Forte Heavy Attack (which can be triggered immediately by performing a Basic Attack after her Resonance Skill), which can convert the last segment when her Forte gauge is full. In case she gets interrupted on that attack however, she may cast it via a Heavy following a teleport Skill as well, provided she has enough Forte to consume.
 With all of the above information, Zhezhi’s rotation becomes clear: She may rotate by activating her Intro skill, filling 1.5 segments of her Forte gauge, then completing a full Basic Attack sequence, filling out the remaining 1.5 segments, using her Resonance Skill and Forte Heavy Attack to convert them all into Imprints, which she will teleport to in quick succession, finishing with her Echo before finally being able to give her 20% Glacio, 25% Skill DMG Amplify Outro to the Main DPS to boost their damage. Her Outro skill has the additional effect of restoring Resonance Energy to the character you switch into - something that is very desired on both DPS characters she typically supports, Carlotta and Jinhsi.
 The gameplay she sports looks fundamentally extremely simplistic - and that statement describes how Zhezhi plays out very accurately. Her ease of use is one of her big selling points, and the above sequence of actions is easy to remember and execute while being quite fast and close to optimal (though it can be optimized via Jump Cancels).
 From a meta standpoint, Zhezhi is nowadays powercrept because she supports powercrept damage dealers. Resonance Skill amplifiers are scarce and the alternatives are bottom tiers in the form of Lumi and Taoqi, but general buffers like Lynae overtake Zhezhi’s spot on most teams outside of her unique use case with Jinhsi since she necessitates Coordinated Attacks. Her ease of use and rare Resonance Skill damage buffing ability make her a strong contender for Jinhsi and Carlotta, but those DPS characters have long since been overshadowed by more recent ones, like Luuk and Hiyuki in the same elements for example.
 In conclusion, even though Zhezhi is one of the very rare choices for Glacio & Skill damage dealers, a lack of something that makes her stand out like strong personal damage, a lightning fast rotation time or high buffing potential make her an overshadowed buffer for DPS characters who are long since
